args.text:
Strategy brain (v1, written before game 1, no game data yet).

Placement phase:
- Prefer junction points with 4 neighbours (5, 11, 14, 20) and midpoints of the middle ring early; they give the most mill lines.
- Block: if the opponent has two on a line with the third point free, place there unless we can close our own mill first.
- Avoid creating two-in-a-row with an open third point that the opponent can take with a block that also builds for them.

Movement phase:
- Aim for a "running mill": a piece that can move out of a mill line and back in, closing a mill every other turn. Keep such a piece adjacent to an empty point that the opponent cannot easily fill.
- Keep pieces in mills when possible (they cannot be removed unless all are in mills).
- When removing, take opponent pieces that threaten an immediate mill first, then pieces that block our lines or sit in their mobility spots.
- Watch mobility: a side with no legal move loses. Try to leave the opponent with few free neighbours.
- Endgame with 3 pieces: flying is allowed; check for double threats.

Draws: 40 turns without a mill after placement, or threefold repetition. If ahead in material, avoid repetition; if behind, repeat to force a draw.

Process: calculate each move by listing opponent's immediate mill threats (two-in-line with empty third, reachable by a neighbour or by placement) before moving.

Basics (first draft, from retro captain A04):
1) Opening placement: prefer junction points with 4 neighbours or 3 (5, 11, 14, 20, then 2, 8, 10, 12, 13, 15, 17, 23). Corners of the outer/middle rings are weaker.

4) When we close a mill, remove an opponent piece that is part of a pending two-in-a-line (breaking their threat) or a mobile piece; pieces in mills are protected unless all are in mills.
5) Movement phase: keep mobility; aim for a piece that can shuttle between two mill lines (running mill). Avoid moves that leave us with no legal move. Watch the 40-turn no-mill draw counter once all placed.
6) With 3 pieces left, we can fly: keep one flying threat ready.
7) Track repetitions; a draw is better than a loss when behind.
Update this brain after each game with what the opponent did and which lines worked.

The retro says O won, so I'm going through what went wrong and turning it into lessons. Early on, the double threats with 4 and 5/6/11/19 worked and forced O to block, which won us pieces. In the placement endgame, though, O built double threats on 16-17-18 and 9-13-18 because I hadn't pre-blocked the fork points, so next time I need to watch for squares where two O lines intersect. Placement:

- Keep at least one extra piece outside the mill when the opponent is about to reach 3.
